title: Verifiable semantics: what before:/after: actually filter
question: If I add after:2026-01-01 to a Google search, what exactly does that filter on? Can I rely on it to get only recently-published information?
ground_truth: Google's help page wording is "documents last updated before/after a particular date" — it filters on last-updated time, not publication date and not the date of the event. A 2019 page re-published today passes it; a correct 2024 page untouched since fails it. Verified at https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/2466433 on 2026-08-13.
why_this_fixture: The intuitive answer ("publication date") is the wrong one, so this measures whether the skill transfers a corrected fact rather than whether the output is well formatted.
